notes: Task was already previously completed (likely before Beads was installed and switched from Trello, and was outdated from the old GAME_CONTEXT.md file). Verified implementation in src/gsdl/core/camera.cr and updated examples/camera_modes.cr to include a toggle for lerping.

title: GSDL Core Foundation
description: Foundation mandates for the GSDL engine core architecture.
notes: Foundation mandates for the GSDL engine core architecture. This epic covers the established, stable systems that form the GSDL framework.

title: Core Structure
description: Game/Scene/Entity hierarchy and execution context.
notes:
• Game owns the main loop, window, and global Draw instance.
• Manages a stack of Scene objects (@scenes : Array(Scene)).
• Execution Context: Game uses an internal @execution_stack to track which scene is currently processing (update/draw). Game.camera automatically resolves to the correct camera based on this context.
• Entity System: Scene and Entity support a parent-child hierarchy via add_child. Updates and draws are automatically propagated through the hierarchy.
• Supports push, pop, replace, and switch for scene transitions.

title: Asset & Data Management
description: AssetManager (Loose/Packed) and GSDL::Data JSON store.
notes:
• AssetManager: Handles loading of assets (textures, audio, fonts, tilemaps, dialogs). Supports 'Loose' assets in debug and 'Packed' assets in release.
• GSDL::Loadable: Unified load_assets pattern for Game and Scene.
• Per-Scene Loading: Scenes can override load_textures, load_audio, etc., for sync or async loading.
• GSDL::Data: JSON-centric key-value store for game state (scores, flags). Supports deep nesting and simple save/load persistence.

title: Rendering & Drawing
description: Z-layered commands, vertex batching, and logical presentation.
notes:
• Command-based drawing system (DrawCommand) with z-indexing, culling, and camera-relative positioning.
• Optimization (Layered Buffer): Commands stored in Z-index buckets (@layers) to avoid heavy sorting.
• Depth Sorting: Within Z-layers, sorted by Y-position using a non-allocating sort! block.
• Vertex Batching: Implement SDL_RenderGeometry to minimize draw calls for shared textures.
• Two-Pass Tinting: Separate buffers for base textures and color-tinted overlays.
• Logical Resolution: Decouples game resolution (e.g., 320x240) from window resolution (e.g., 1080p).
• Scaling: Handled via SDL_SetRenderLogicalPresentation (Letterbox, Stretch, etc.).
• Visual Offsets: GSDL::SpriteBase separates physical base (draw_y) from visual rendering position (render_offset_y) to support height/depth effects without breaking Y-sorting.

title: TileMap System
description: Tiled JSON/TMX support and TileObjectFactory.
notes:
• Supports Tiled .json and .tmx formats.
• Multi-Layer & Object Support: TileLayer and ObjectGroup layers.
• Tileset Management: GSDL::Tileset handles textures and solid_tiles collision metadata.
• Tile Objects: GSDL::TileObject and TileObjectFactory handle rectangles, ellipses, points, and custom tiled objects.

title: Collision System
description: AABB, Circle, and SAT support via Collidable.
notes:
• Custom collision system supporting AABB (Rect), Circle, and SAT (Polygon) checks via GSDL::Collidable.
• GSDL::CollisionSpace: Manages a flat list of Collidable entities (usually via GSDL::SceneCollisions).

title: UI & RichText
description: Component suite and texture-baked RichText.
notes:
• FontManager & DialogManager (YAML-based structured dialogue).
• UI Components: Button, ProgressBar, Slider, TabContainer, TextInput, ScrollTextView.
• RichText: Inline colored/styled text with texture baking strategy.
• RichTextTyped: Typewriter-style reveals for rich text.
• HUD: Screen-space overlays with anchoring and padding support.

title: Input & Tweens
description: Action mapping, MultiTapTracker, and Tweenable presets.
notes:
• Input: GSDL::Input and GSDL::Keys with action-based mapping.
• MultiTapTracker: Handles double/triple tap detection.
• Animation: GSDL::Animation and AnimationPlayer for frame-based sprites.
• Particles: GSDL::ParticleEmitter and GSDL::Particle for VFX.
• Movement Controllers: GSDL::TopDownController, PlatformerController, PhysicsController, and VerticalScrollController.
• Tweens: GSDL::Tweenable for transitions (x, y, scale, color, tint) with presets (flash, shake, pulse, spin).

title: Camera System
description: View transformation, modes, and screen shake.
notes:
• View transformation (x, y, zoom).
• Modes: Fixed, AutoScroll, CenterOnTarget (with/without boundary), and Manual.
• Built-in screen shake via Tweenable integration.

title: Distribution & Packaging
description: gsdl-packer and automated OS-specific bundling.
notes:
• gsdl-packer: Standalone tool to bundle assets into assets.pack binary.
• release packaging: Automated bundle creation for macOS (.app), Windows (.exe + DLLs), and Linux (.tar.gz).

title: Refine and Optimize RichText & RichTextTyped
description:
**Objective**: Perform a comprehensive audit of RichText and RichTextTyped to ensure their manual segment-based baking logic is robust and optimized for the oversampling architecture.
**Details**:
- **Oversampling Consistency**: Verify that oversample_ratio is applied uniformly across all segments and that coordinate mapping between logical layout and oversampled baking is pixel-perfect.
- **Bake Performance**: RichTextTyped currently re-bakes the entire texture on every character/word typed. Investigate if performance impacts are significant at high oversample ratios and consider 'incremental baking' if necessary.
- **Tag Verification**: Rigorously test style tags (<b>, <i>, c:) under various scales and rotations to ensure the custom layout engine doesn't introduce artifacts.
- **Alignment Support**: Ensure that Center and Right alignment in RichText handles multi-line segment layouts correctly.
notes: Optimized RichText/RichTextTyped by decoupling layout and baking passes. Introduced `Text::OversampleRatio` constant (default 4.0). Aligned Text/RichText draw math with SpriteBase/Sprite for engine-wide consistency. Verified high-quality scaling and efficient typing animations in examples.

title: Spatial Querying
description: Implement spatial partitioning for CollisionSpace optimization.
notes: Optimized CollisionSpace grid refresh. Moved refresh_grid call from query path to Scene#update, ensuring grid is rebuilt exactly once per frame for scenes using SceneCollisions.

title: Optimize Dynamic Text Components
description:
**Objective**: Ensure that components with frequently changing text (TextTyped, NumberFlash, TextBox) are optimized to prevent performance degradation from excessive texture re-baking.
**Details**:
- **Bake Throttle**: For components like TextTyped, verify that the re-baking frequency is tied correctly to the typing speed and doesn't waste cycles.
- **Size Stability**: Audit NumberFlash to ensure that rapidly changing numbers (e.g., '100' -> '1000') don't cause jarring layout shifts due to changing baked texture dimensions.
- **Text Selection/Input**: Verify TextBox and TextInput interaction logic (cursor placement, selection boxes) now that they must map logical mouse coordinates back to an oversampled texture layout.
notes: Optimized dynamic text components. TextTyped now uses `visible_characters` to avoid re-baking during animation. NumberFlash uses the new `opacity` property to fade out via texture alpha mod instead of color changes. Added `cursor_pos` helper to Text for accurate logical coordinate mapping. Verified with text_input and full examples.

title: Graphics: Unified Runtime Texture Atlas
description:
Goal: Consolidate all individual textures into one or more master GPU textures at runtime. This maximizes batching efficiency while optimizing VRAM usage by using smart Power-of-Two (POT) scaling.

## Technical Specifications

### 1. Affected Files
- src/gsdl/gfx/texture.cr: Add atlas_rect : FRect? and atlas_handle : SDL3::Texture?.
- src/gsdl/gfx/texture_manager.cr: Implement finalize_atlas logic, shelf-packing, and master texture storage.
- src/gsdl/gfx/draw.cr: Update add_texture_to_batch to utilize atlas UV coordinates.
- src/gsdl/core/game.cr: Trigger TextureManager.finalize_atlas after load_assets in the _init sequence.

### 2. Implementation Requirements
- Smart Sizing: The atlas should start at the smallest possible POT size (e.g. 512x512) and grow dynamically (1024x1024, 2048x1024, etc.) based on the results of the packing algorithm.
- Hardware Limits: Use SDL_GetRendererInfo to respect the GPU's max_texture_width and max_texture_height. If assets exceed this limit, spawn additional atlas pages.
- Padding: Include 2px of transparent padding between assets to prevent texture bleeding.
- Universal Mode: Runs in both Debug and Release modes.

### 3. UV Calculation Logic
In Draw#add_texture_to_batch, normalize coordinates against the specific atlas page handle:

```crystal
if a_rect = command.texture.atlas_rect
  atlas_handle = command.texture.atlas_handle.not_nil!
  atlas_w, atlas_h = atlas_handle.size
  
  base_x, base_y = a_rect.x, a_rect.y
  
  if src = command.source_rect
    u1 = (base_x + src.x) / atlas_w
    v1 = (base_y + src.y) / atlas_h
    u2 = (base_x + src.x + src.w) / atlas_w
    v2 = (base_y + src.y + src.h) / atlas_h
  else
    u1 = base_x / atlas_w
    v1 = base_y / atlas_h
    u2 = (base_x + a_rect.w) / atlas_w
    v2 = (base_y + a_rect.h) / atlas_h
  end
end
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TextureManager produces the smallest possible POT atlas that fits all assets.
- [ ] Batcher correctly identifies sub-textures and switches atlas pages only when the master handle changes.
- [ ] Zero visual regressions in texture rendering compared to individual texture loading.
notes: Implemented dynamic runtime texture atlas packing (shelf algorithm). Updated Draw and TextureManager for atlas-aware rendering and batching. Verified via performance_stress.cr (significant flush count reduction).

title: Performance: Batch Flush vs. Command Metrics
description:
Goal: Differentiate between total draw calls (API requests) and actual hardware 'flushes' (when texture changes or buffer capacity is reached).

## Implementation
- Add @current_flush_count and @last_flush_count to GSDL::Draw.
- Increment flush count inside Draw#flush_batch (only if vertex buffer is non-empty).
- Display 'flushes' alongside 'commands' in the GSDL::HUDPerformance overlay (src/gsdl/ui/hud.cr).

## Success Metric
Healthy batching should show flushes significantly lower than commands in standard scenes.
notes: Extended implementation to include Commands and Flushes in the GSDL::Performance session report and rolling averages in HUDPerformance (when performance_monitoring_enabled is true). Verified with performance_stress.cr.

title: UI Layout & Alignment Audit
description:
**Objective**: Verify that high-level UI components correctly align, scale, and pad their internal baked Text objects.
**Details**:
- **Centering Accuracy**: Audit Button and Message centering logic. Since baked textures may have slightly different dimensions than the logical font metrics, verify that visual centering remains perfect.
- **Wrapping & Resizing**: Verify DialogBox, Notification, and HUD correctly respond to text changes that trigger dimension updates in the underlying baked textures.
- **Logical Presentation**: Ensure HUD elements remain crisp when the game's logical presentation or window size changes, verifying that they don't accidentally re-bake using the wrong DPI or scale factor.
notes: Completed comprehensive audit of UI components (Button, Message, DialogBox, Notification, HUD). All components correctly leverage the logical dimensions of the new baked-text system. Introduced `visible_characters` and `opacity` to base Text class to optimize dynamic UI elements (TextTyped, NumberFlash), significantly reducing re-bake frequency. Verified pixel-perfect alignment and scaling across all UI examples.

title: SDF Font Support by Default
description: Enable Signed Distance Field (SDF) rendering by default for all fonts loaded via GSDL to ensure high-fidelity text at any scale.
notes: Enabled SDF rendering by default for all fonts loaded via GSDL::FontManager. Updated load, load_from_memory, and get methods to explicitly set font.sdf = true. Verified with a test script and by building examples/full.cr.

title: Scene Persistence & Snapshot Engine
description:
Implement a scene-specific persistence system to capture dynamic game state (e.g., entity positions, health, local variables) distinct from global game metadata.

## Architectural Approach
- Implement a `GSDL::Saveable` module that can be mixed into entities or components that need to be persisted.
- Entities must implement a `save_state : Hash(String, JSON::Any)` method for serialization.
- Extend `SceneManager` to traverse dynamic entities and collect their state using the `Saveable` interface.
- During save operations, `SceneManager` will ask each registered "Saveable" entity to serialize itself and merge the result with the current room ID into a "Scene Snapshot" object.
- Structure the persistence payload to contain both global data (from `GameData`) and transient scene snapshots:
  {
    "global": { ... }, 
    "scene": { "room_id": "...", "entities": { ... } }
  }
- Utilize the existing binary persistence logic (Zlib + XOR + CRC32) for the full snapshot.

## Requirements
- Add a new `save_scene_state` example to `examples/` demonstrating entity state capture, saving, and reloading.
- Ensure state loading can reconstruct entity positions and local variables within a scene.
- Maintain backward compatibility where scenes without state are handled gracefully.
notes:
# Architectural Summary: Scene Persistence Strategy

## Decision
- We will keep the library core lean and avoid forcing `GSDL::Saveable` on internal or non-state classes (e.g., textures, engine internals, shaders).
- Future scalability relies on consumers including `GSDL::Saveable` in their own project entities and overriding `save_state`/`load_state` on an as-needed basis.

## Rationale
- Implementing `Saveable` globally creates significant maintenance debt, schema versioning issues, and dead code for users not utilizing persistence.
- Monolithic serialization (forcing everything to be saveable) would make versioning and schema migrations nearly impossible to manage long-term.

## Developer Best Practices
- **Selective Implementation**: Only implement `Saveable` for dynamic game-state classes (e.g., Players, NPCs, interactive objects).
- **Versioning**: Avoid hard-coding schemas across many files. If a global schema change is required, handle it in a centralized migration layer or via the `GameData` versioning system implemented in `proj-v2t`.
- **User Empowerment**: GSDL should remain library-agnostic and clean, providing the `Saveable` interface but letting the consumer decide which classes are persisted.

title: Unify Rotatable Text in TextBase
description: Refactor the text system to support rotation directly within GSDL::TextBase and its children, rendering GSDL::TextRotated obsolete. This leverages SDF font properties and the SDL_RenderTextureRotated API to ensure text remains sharp and smooth when rotated. NOTE: SDL_RenderTextureRotated must be implemented in sdl3.cr bindings first.
notes: Refactored the text system to support rotation directly in GSDL::Text. Added rotation and origin-based center of rotation to GSDL::TextBase. Updated GSDL::Text to handle rotation by caching an internal texture when rotation is non-zero, leveraging the 'bake' method. Removed the now obsolete GSDL::TextRotated class and updated all examples to use GSDL::Text instead. Verified with examples/tween.cr and library-wide build of examples/full.cr.

title: Binary Persistence
description:
Goal: Transition GSDL game state persistence from plaintext JSON to a robust, compressed binary format to prevent trivial user modification and prepare for production-grade save management.

## Technical Specifications

### 1. Binary File Structure
The new format should utilize a structured binary header (12-16 bytes) before the payload:
- Magic Number (4 bytes): 0x4753444C (ASCII 'GSDL') to verify file type.
- Format Version (4 bytes): UInt32 to handle future migrations.
- Checksum (4 bytes): A CRC32 or Adler32 hash of the payload to ensure data integrity.
- Payload: The @data hash serialized to JSON, then compressed using Compress::Zlib.

### 2. Implementation Requirements
- Smart Loading: Update GSDL::GameData#load to detect the format automatically. If the first 4 bytes match the magic number, process as binary; otherwise, fallback to legacy JSON for backward compatibility.
- Atomic Writes: Implement 'Save-and-Swap' (write to .tmp, then rename) to prevent file corruption during save operations.
- Obfuscation: Apply a bitwise XOR transformation to the compressed payload to further discourage hex-editing.

### 3. API Enhancements
- Add GSDL::GameData#save_binary(path) and GSDL::GameData#save_json(path) for development flexibility.
- Ensure GSDL::Data.save defaults to the new binary format.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GSDL::Data.save produces a non-human-readable file.
- [ ] GSDL::Data.load correctly restores state from both new binary and old JSON formats.
- [ ] Corrupted save files (invalid checksum/magic) are handled with clear error logging.
- [ ] Verified performance: No noticeable lag during save operations for typical game state sizes.
notes: Implemented binary persistence with Zlib compression, XOR obfuscation, and CRC32 checksums. Added Save-and-Swap atomic writes. Maintained legacy JSON support. Verified with new 'examples/save_data.cr' and full build.

title: Refactor GSDL::Text for Baked Textures & Oversampling
description:
# Implementation Plan: Refactor GSDL::Text for Baked Textures & Oversampling

## Objective
Replace the current `SDL3::TTF::Text`-based rendering in `GSDL::Text` and `GSDL::TextBase` with a custom baked-texture approach. This will utilize oversampling to produce high-quality text scaling and rotation, rendering text to a `Surface`, converting it to a `Texture`, and drawing it using the existing `Draw#texture_rotated` batching infrastructure.

## Key Files & Context
- `src/gsdl/ui/text_base.cr`: Will be deleted.
- `src/gsdl/ui/text.cr`: Will be completely rewritten to inherit from `Entity` directly and manage its own texture baking.
- `src/gsdl/gfx/draw.cr`: Needs to be stripped of `DrawTextCommand`, `text_engine`, and direct `text` rendering methods.
- `src/gsdl/ui/font.cr`: Contains the `size=` property and `render_text_blended` methods needed for oversampling.
- Dependent UI components (`src/gsdl/ui/rich_text.cr`, `text_typed.cr`, `text_box.cr`, etc.): May need minor adjustments or commenting out *only* if they fail to compile.
- Examples: May need commenting out *only* if they fail to compile.

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Task Tracking Registration
- Create a new `br` task containing this entire plan and start the task to record the development context.

### 2. Draw System Cleanup (`src/gsdl/gfx/draw.cr`)
- Remove the `DrawTextCommand` class.
- Remove the `def text(text : Text)` rendering methods.
- Remove `@text_engine` and its initialization/destruction logic.
- Remove any lingering `TextEngine` references from `Draw`.

### 3. Refactor `GSDL::Text` (`src/gsdl/ui/text.cr`)
- Delete `src/gsdl/ui/text_base.cr`.
- Rewrite `src/gsdl/ui/text.cr`:
  - Inherit directly from `Entity` and include `Centerable`.
  - Add configurable property `@oversample_ratio : Float32 = 4_f32`.
  - Retain `text`, `font`, `color`, `align`, `wrap_width`, `rotation`, `z_index`, `origin`, and `scale` properties.
  - Implement a `bake!` method:
    - Destroy any existing `@texture`.
    - Skip baking if `@text` is empty.
    - Save the original font size: `original_size = @font.size`.
    - Temporarily scale the font: `@font.size = original_size * @oversample_ratio`.
    - Apply font alignment (`@font.align = @align`).
    - Render to surface: Use `@font.render_text_blended_wrapped` if `@wrap_width` is set, otherwise `@font.render_text_blended`.
    - Convert `Surface` to `Texture` via `Game.draw.create_texture(surface)` (or `SDL3::Texture.from_surface`).
    - Enable blend mode on the texture.
    - Restore the original font size: `@font.size = original_size`.
    - Destroy the surface.
  - Call `bake!` during `initialize` and whenever relevant properties (`text`, `font`, `color`, `wrap_width`, etc.) change.
  - Implement the `draw(draw : Draw)` method:
    - If `@texture` exists, calculate the destination rectangle. The size should be `(texture.width / @oversample_ratio) * scale_x` and `(texture.height / @oversample_ratio) * scale_y`.
    - Use `draw.texture_rotated` with the calculated `dest_rect`, `rotation`, `center_point_from_origin`, and `z_index`.
  - Ensure `#destroy` cleans up the baked texture.

### 4. Compilation Mitigation
- Run `make build` or `crystal build examples/text.cr` (and others) to identify compilation failures.
- If UI components (like `RichText`, `TextBox`) or examples fail to compile because they rely on the removed `TextBase` or `SDL3::TTF::Text` methods, modify them minimally or comment out the failing code blocks to restore compilation.
- *Constraint*: Do not comment out code if it compiles but is functionally broken; only fix compilation errors.

## Verification & Testing
- Run `crystal run examples/text.cr` (or an equivalent text scaling example) to verify that text renders correctly, responds to scaling and rotation without pixelation, and that memory is properly managed (no texture leaks on text updates).
- Ensure the project builds successfully without `TextEngine` or `DrawTextCommand` errors.
notes: Refactored GSDL::Text to use baked textures with oversampling (default 4x). Removed TextBase and DrawTextCommand, simplifying the draw system. Implemented multi-line support in GSDL::Text by compositing line surfaces using a new Surface#blit method. Updated RichText and other UI components to align with the new Text architecture. Verified with examples/text.cr and examples/full.cr.

title: Enhanced Renderer Configuration
description: Optimize SDL_Renderer for GSDL's 'Standard Indie' aesthetic, ensuring pixel-perfect sprites, integer scaling, and VSync synchronization.
notes: Optimized SDL_Renderer for GSDL's 'Standard Indie' aesthetic. Set default scale quality to 'nearest' in GSDL::Draw. Configured logical presentation to use IntegerScale for pixel-perfect scaling. Applied vsync setting to the renderer in GSDL::Game initialization. These changes, combined with the centralization of SDF in GSDL::Font, fix the blurry text issue while maintaining the option for high-fidelity rendering.
